cards.grammarNote:
Basic sentences follow **Subject + Verb + Object**, just like English:
**我**(I) + **吃**(eat) + **饭**(rice) = **我吃饭**. Verbs never change for person or tense.
cards.englishPhrase: I eat rice, he drinks tea.
cards.phraseRomanized: Wǒ chī fàn, tā hē chá.

table.title: Word order: Subject + Verb + Object
table.note: 我吃饭 = I eat rice. Verbs never change for person or tense.

cards.english: I am a student. (是 links two nouns)
cards.grammarNote:
**是**(shì) links two nouns: A **是** B = 'A is B'.
**我是学生**(I'm a student), **他是医生**(he's a doctor).
Don't put **是** before an adjective — use **很** instead.

table.title: A 是 shì B = A is B (links two nouns)
rows: 我是学生 wǒ shì xuéshēng
他是医生 tā shì yīshēng
我不是老师 wǒ bú shì lǎoshī
table.note: Negate with 不是. Never put 是 before an adjective — use 很.

cards.english: I am happy. (adjective takes 很, not 是)
cards.grammarNote:
Adjectives act like verbs — **don't** add **是** before them. Use **很**(hěn):
**我很高兴**(I'm happy), **我很累**(I'm tired). Here **很** just links; it only means 'very' when stressed.

contrast.prompt: 'I am happy' — 是 or 很?

a.term: 我很高兴 wǒ hěn gāoxìng
a.gloss: ✓ an adjective takes 很, not 是

b.gloss: ✗ never 是 before an adjective

cards.english: Are you well? (吗 makes a yes/no question)
cards.grammarNote:
Add **吗**(ma) to the end of a statement to make a yes/no question:
**你好** → **你好吗？**(are you well?), **你是学生吗？**(are you a student?). Word order doesn't change.

cloze.prompt: make it a yes/no question (你好 = you are well)

cards.english: What do you want? (question word stays put)
cards.grammarNote:
Question words sit **where the answer goes** — they don't move to the front:
**你想要什么？**(you want what?), **他是谁？**(he is who?). The answer just replaces the question word.
cards.englishPhrase: What do you want to eat?

produce.concept: Question words stay where the answer goes — they don't move to the front
produce.task: ask: you want what? (= what do you want?)
produce.answer: 你想要什么？nǐ xiǎng yào shénme?
produce.gloss: 什么 sits in the object slot; the answer just replaces it. 他是谁？= who is he?

cards.grammarNote:
Count nouns with a **measure word** between the number and the noun:
**一个苹果**(one apple), **两个鸡蛋**(two eggs). **个**(gè) is the general measure word; drinks use **杯**: **一杯茶**(a cup of tea).

table.title: Number + measure word + noun
rows: 一个苹果 yí gè píngguǒ
两个鸡蛋 liǎng gè jīdàn
table.note: 个 gè is the default measure word; some nouns take their own (本 běn for books).

cards.english: I'll have a coffee. (要 to order)
cards.grammarNote:
**要**(yào) = want / would like — the everyday verb for ordering:
**我要一杯咖啡**(I'll have a coffee). **杯**(bēi) is the measure word for cups and glasses.
cards.englishPhrase: I'll have a cup of tea, thanks.
cards.phraseRomanized: Wǒ yào yì bēi chá, xièxie.

produce.concept: 要 yào = 'I'll have' — the everyday verb for ordering
produce.task: order: one coffee
produce.answer: 我要一杯咖啡 wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi
produce.gloss: 杯 bēi is the measure word for cups and glasses.

cards.grammarNote:
**想**(xiǎng) + verb = want to do something:
**我想吃**(I want to eat), **我想喝茶**(I want to drink tea). Softer than **要**, which is more 'I'll have / I want'.

contrast.prompt: 想 xiǎng vs 要 yào

a.gloss: 想 + verb = want TO DO (a wish, softer)

b.term: 我要一杯咖啡 wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi
b.gloss: 要 + noun = want / I'll have (ordering)

cards.grammarNote:
**好**(hǎo, good) + a verb = pleasant to do:
**好吃**(good to eat = delicious, for food), **好喝**(good to drink — for tea/coffee), **好看**(good-looking).

table.title: 好 hǎo (good) + verb = pleasant to…
rows: 好吃 hǎochī — good to eat
好喝 hǎohē — good to drink
好看 hǎokàn — good to look at
table.note: A productive pattern: 好 + a verb.

cards.english: I am at home. (在 for location)
cards.grammarNote:
**在**(zài) = to be at / located at:
**我在家**(I'm at home), **他在学校**(he's at school). Structure: Subject + **在** + place.

table.title: Location: Subject + 在 zài + place
rows: 他在学校 tā zài xuéxiào
table.note: 在 = to be at / located at. 哪儿 nǎr = where.

cards.english: I eat at the restaurant. (在 + place before the verb)
cards.grammarNote:
To say where an action happens, put **在 + place before the verb**:
**我在餐厅吃饭**(I at-restaurant eat) — not after the verb like English.

contrast.prompt: Where does 在+place go? (I eat at the restaurant)

a.term: 我在餐厅吃饭 wǒ zài cāntīng chī fàn
a.gloss: ✓ 在+place goes BEFORE the verb

b.gloss: ✗ not after the verb like English

cards.english: I go to the park. (去 needs no 'to')
cards.grammarNote:
**去**(qù, to go) attaches straight to a place — there's no word for 'to':
**我去公园**(I go park), **我去学校**(I go to school). Put a time word before **去** to say when.
cards.englishPhrase: In the morning I go to the park.

produce.concept: 去 qù (to go) attaches straight to a place — there's no word for 'to'
produce.task: say: I go to the park
produce.answer: 我去公园 wǒ qù gōngyuán
produce.gloss: 我去学校 = I go to school. A time word goes before 去.

cards.english: in the room (在 … 里 wraps the place)
cards.grammarNote:
Position words wrap the noun: **在 + place + 里/上/下**:
**在房间里**(in the room), **在桌子上**(on the table), **在床下**(under the bed).
cards.englishPhrase: The cat is in the room.

table.title: 在 + place + 里/上/下 (position words)
rows: 在房间里 zài fángjiān lǐ
在桌子上 zài zhuōzi shàng
table.note: 里 inside · 上 on top · 下 under — the position word follows the noun.

cards.grammarNote:
State your job with **是**(shì): Subject + **是** + job.
**我是医生**(I'm a doctor), **她是学生**(she's a student). To ask: **你是做什么的？**(what do you do?).

produce.concept: State your job with 是: Subject + 是 + job
produce.task: say: I am a doctor
produce.answer: 我是医生 wǒ shì yīshēng
produce.gloss: Ask 你是做什么的？nǐ shì zuò shénme de? = what do you do?

cards.grammarNote:
**喜欢**(xǐhuān, to like) can be followed straight by a verb = 'like doing':
**我喜欢阅读**(I like reading), **我喜欢跑步**(I like running). No 'to' or '-ing' change needed.

produce.concept: 喜欢 xǐhuān (to like) + verb = like doing
produce.task: say: I like reading
produce.answer: 我喜欢阅读 wǒ xǐhuān yuèdú
produce.gloss: No 'to' or '-ing' — just 喜欢 + verb. 我喜欢跑步 = I like running.

cards.english: I am working. (在 + verb = happening now)
cards.grammarNote:
Put **在**(zài) before a verb to show it's happening right now:
**我在工作**(I'm working), **他在唱歌**(he's singing). It's the '-ing' of Chinese.

cards.english: I can swim. (会 = a learned skill)
cards.grammarNote:
**会**(huì) = can, for skills you've learned:
**我会游泳**(I can swim), **我会说中文**(I can speak Chinese). Compare **能**(néng) = able / allowed in a situation.
cards.phraseRomanized: Wǒ huì yóuyǒng, nǐ huì ma?

produce.concept: 会 huì = can, for a skill you've learned
produce.task: say: I can swim
produce.answer: 我会游泳 wǒ huì yóuyǒng
produce.gloss: 会 = learned skills. 我会说中文 = I can speak Chinese.

cards.english: I am happy. (很 + adjective, no 是)
cards.grammarNote:
Describe a mood with **很**(hěn) + adjective — **no 是**:
**我很快乐**(I'm happy), **我很累**(I'm tired). **很** links subject to adjective; it only means 'very' when stressed.

cloze.prompt: I'm happy (mood → 很 + adjective, no 是)

cards.english: I feel tired. (觉得 = feel / think that)
cards.grammarNote:
**觉得**(juéde) = to feel / think that — introduces a feeling or opinion:
**我觉得很累**(I feel tired), **我觉得这个很好**(I think this is good). Follow it with an adjective (+很) or a full clause.

produce.concept: 觉得 juéde = to feel / think that — introduces an opinion
produce.task: say: I feel tired
produce.answer: 我觉得很累 wǒ juéde hěn lèi
produce.gloss: Follow it with a full comment: 我觉得这个很好 = I think this is good.

cards.english: I'm a little nervous. (有点儿 + adjective)
cards.grammarNote:
**有点儿**(yǒudiǎnr) + adjective = 'a little / somewhat', usually for something undesirable:
**有点儿紧张**(a bit nervous), **有点儿累**(a little tired). It goes before the adjective.

cloze.prompt: I'm a little nervous (有点儿 + adjective, usually negative)

cards.grammarNote:
**太**(tài) … **了**(le) wraps an adjective = 'too / so':
**太累了**(too tired), **太好了**(great! — lit. too good). A strong feeling, often exclaimed.

cloze.prompt: I'm SO tired! ('too …' → 太 … 了)

cards.grammarNote:
**的**(de) links a possessor to a thing, like 's / my:
**我的手**(my hand), **他的眼睛**(his eyes). For close relationships you can drop **的**: **我妈**(my mom).

produce.concept: 的 de links owner to thing (like 's / my)
produce.task: say: my hand
produce.gloss: 他的眼睛 = his eyes. Close relations can drop 的: 我妈 = my mom.

cards.grammarNote:
To say a body part hurts, name it then add **疼**(téng, to ache):
**我头疼**(my head hurts, lit. 'I head ache'), **我牙疼**(toothache). This topic-then-comment order is very common.

produce.concept: Say what hurts: (I) + body part + 疼 téng (to ache)
produce.task: say: my head hurts
produce.gloss: Literally 'I head ache' — topic then comment. 我牙疼 = toothache.

cards.grammarNote:
A two-syllable adjective takes **的** before the noun it describes:
**软的皮肤**(soft skin), **健康的身体**(healthy body). Single-syllable adjectives often skip **的**: **大手**(big hand).

table.title: Longer adjective + 的 de + noun
rows: 软的皮肤 ruǎn de pífū
健康的身体 jiànkāng de shēntǐ
红的苹果 hóng de píngguǒ
table.note: Single-syllable adjectives often skip 的 (好人 = a good person).

cards.english: two hands (只 counts hands, eyes, ears)
cards.grammarNote:
Paired body parts often take the measure word **只**(zhī):
**两只手**(two hands), **两只眼睛**(two eyes), **一只耳朵**(one ear). Use **两**(liǎng), not 二, before a measure word.

cloze.prompt: two hands (只 counts hands, eyes, ears)

packs.name: 了 · 过 · 在 · 着 — Aspect Particles

cards.grammarNote: **动词 + 了** marks a completed action. It does NOT mean past tense — it means the action is finished.

produce.concept: 了 after a verb = the action is completed.
produce.task: say 'I ate' from 吃 (eat)
produce.gloss: 吃 (eat) + 了 = 吃了 (ate / have eaten)

cards.grammarNote: Add **了** for a finished action; leave it off for habits or general facts.

contrast.prompt: One time, completed — or a general habit?

a.gloss: Wǒ hē le chá — I drank the tea (completed)

b.gloss: Wǒ hē chá — I drink tea (habit, general)

cards.grammarNote: Ask about a completed action with **Verb + 了 + 吗**. Answer 吃了 (yes) or 没吃 (no).

cloze.prompt: Have you eaten? (yes/no question about a completed action)

cards.grammarNote: Negate a completed action with **没**, and **drop 了**: 我没吃 (never 没吃了).

contrast.prompt: How do you say the action did NOT happen?

a.gloss: Wǒ chī le — I ate (completed)

b.gloss: Wǒ méi chī — I didn't eat (drop 了, use 没)

cards.grammarNote: **了** at the end of a sentence marks a **change of state** — a new situation that wasn't true before.

table.title: 了 at the end = a new situation
rows: 我不饿 wǒ bù è — I'm not hungry
我饿了 wǒ è le — I'm hungry now
table.note: Sentence-final 了 signals a change: something is different now.

cards.grammarNote: **Adjective + 了** = became / now is: 累了 (got tired), 好了 (all better / ready).

produce.concept: Sentence-final 了 = a change just happened.
produce.task: say 'I'm tired now' with 累 (tired)
produce.gloss: Wǒ lèi le — I'm tired now (wasn't before).

cards.grammarNote: 了 after the **verb** = completion. 了 at the **end** = a new situation. Same character, two jobs.

contrast.prompt: Two jobs of 了 — which is which?

a.gloss: Wǒ chī le fàn — verb+了 = completed action

b.gloss: Wǒ è le — sentence-final 了 = change of state

cards.grammarNote: **快 … 了** = about to happen very soon: 饭快好了 (almost ready).

cloze.prompt: The meal is almost ready (about to happen)

cards.grammarNote: **动词 + 过** marks an **experience** — you've done it at least once. 过 is toneless here (guo).

produce.concept: Verb + 过 = have done it before (at least once in life).
produce.task: say 'I've eaten hotpot' with 吃 (eat) 火锅 (hotpot)
produce.gloss: Wǒ chī guo huǒguō — I've had hotpot before.

cards.grammarNote: **了** = a specific completed action. **过** = you've done it before at some point.

contrast.prompt: A finished event, or a life experience?

a.gloss: Wǒ chī le — I ate (just now, completed)

b.gloss: Wǒ chī guo — I've eaten (before, experience)

cards.grammarNote: Ask about experience with **Verb + 过 … 吗？**

cloze.prompt: Have you ever been to the beach?

cards.englishPhrase: Have you ever been to the beach?

cards.grammarNote: Negate experience with **没 … 过** (keep 过!): 没去过 = have never gone.

contrast.prompt: Say you've NEVER done it

a.gloss: Wǒ qù guo — I've been (there)

b.gloss: Wǒ méi qù guo — I've never been

cards.english: 了 vs 过 in the negative
cards.grammarNote: 了 disappears under 没; 过 does not.

table.title: 过 vs 了 in the negative
rows: 没吃 méi chī — didn't eat
没吃过 méi chī guo — never eaten
table.note: 了 disappears under 没; 过 stays.

cards.grammarNote: 过 = at least once in your life; keep 过 even in the negative.

table.title: 过 — experience aspect
rows: 去过 qù guo — have been
没去过 méi qù guo — never been
去过吗 qù guo ma — have you ever been?
table.note: 过 = at least once in your life; keep 过 even in the negative.

cards.grammarNote: **在 + 动词** = ongoing action. (Essentials: 我在工作 = I'm working.)

produce.concept: 在 + verb = an action happening right now.
produce.task: say 'I am eating' with 吃 (eat)
produce.gloss: Wǒ zài chī fàn — I'm eating (right now).

cards.grammarNote: Put **在** before the verb to show the action is unfolding right now.

table.title: Ongoing action: Subject + 在 + Verb
table.note: 他在吃饭 = He is eating right now.

cards.english: 在 = place vs 在 = action
cards.grammarNote: **在 + place** = location. **在 + verb** = an action in progress. (在家吃饭 = eating at home.)

contrast.prompt: 在 = location, or 在 = ongoing action?

a.gloss: Wǒ zài jiā — I'm at home (在 + place)

b.gloss: Wǒ zài chī fàn — I'm eating (在 + verb)

cards.grammarNote: **正在** = 在 with extra emphasis on this very moment.

produce.concept: 正在 + verb stresses 'right at this moment'.
produce.task: say 'He is working right now' with 工作 (work)
produce.gloss: Tā zhèngzài gōngzuò — he's working right now.

cards.grammarNote: Negate an ongoing action with **没(在)**: 没在工作 = not working (now).

cloze.prompt: I'm not working right now; I'm resting

cards.phraseRomanized: Wǒ méi zài gōngzuò, wǒ zài xiūxi.
cards.englishPhrase: I'm not working right now; I'm resting.

cards.grammarNote: **在** = an action unfolding. **着** = a state that continues. 在 focuses on 'doing', 着 on 'staying in a state'.

contrast.prompt: An action in progress, or a continuing state?

a.gloss: Tā zài kàn — he is looking (action happening)

b.gloss: Tā kàn zhe — he keeps looking (ongoing state)

cards.grammarNote: **动词 + 着** shows the state continues: 等着 = waiting (and still waiting).

produce.concept: Verb + 着 = the action/state continues.
produce.task: say 'I'm waiting for you' with 等 (wait)
produce.gloss: Wǒ děng zhe nǐ — I'm waiting for you.

cards.grammarNote: 笑着说 = said (it) smilingly — 着 links a continuing manner to the main verb.

cloze.prompt: He said it with a smile (smiling)

cards.englishPhrase: He said it with a smile.

cards.english: 了 · 过 · 在 · 着 side by side
cards.word: 了 / 过 / 在 / 着
cards.grammarNote: Four aspect markers, four jobs: **了** done, **过** done before at least once, **在** doing right now, **着** staying in a state.

table.title: The four aspect markers
table.note: 了 = finished; 过 = ever done; 在 = happening now; 着 = ongoing state.

cards.grammarNote: **不 + verb/adjective** = general 'not': habits, preferences, the future. (不好 = not good.)

produce.concept: 不 = not — for habits, the present, the future, and adjectives.
produce.task: say 'I don't eat meat' with 吃 (eat) 肉 (meat)
produce.gloss: Wǒ bù chī ròu — I don't eat meat.

cards.grammarNote: 不 negates habits, states, adjectives, and future intentions.

table.title: 不 — when to use it
rows: 我不喝茶 — I don't drink tea
table.note: 不 negates habits, states, adjectives, and future intentions.

cards.grammarNote: Adjectives are negated with **不**: 不好 = not good.
不去 = won't go (a decision about now or the future).

produce.concept: 不 also negates what you won't / don't want to do.
produce.task: say 'I won't go' with 去 (go)
produce.gloss: Wǒ bù qù — I'm not going / I won't go.

cards.grammarNote: **没** negates a finished action or existence/有.

table.title: 没(有) — for completed actions & 'have'
rows: 没吃 méi chī — didn't eat
没有工作 méiyǒu gōngzuò — has no job
table.note: 没 negates a finished action or 有 (have).

cards.english: 不 vs 没 — the core split
cards.grammarNote: **不** = general/future 'not'. **没** = a specific action didn't happen.

contrast.prompt: 不 or 没 — habit vs completed?

a.gloss: Wǒ bù chī — I don't eat (it) / won't

b.gloss: Wǒ méi chī — I didn't eat / haven't eaten

cards.grammarNote: A completed action that didn't happen uses **没**, not 不.
**有** is always negated by **没(有)** — never 不有.

contrast.prompt: 'have' vs 'don't have'

a.gloss: yǒu gōngzuò — has a job

b.gloss: méiyǒu gōngzuò — doesn't have a job

cards.grammarNote: 没有 = don't/doesn't have. 不有 is wrong.
Only 有 forces 没; adjectives and habits take 不.

table.title: 不 or 没?
table.note: Pick by meaning: general 不, completed/有 没.

cards.grammarNote: 没买 = didn't buy. (Positive completed = 买了; the negative drops 了.)

produce.concept: A finished action that didn't happen: 没 + verb.
produce.task: say 'I didn't buy it' with 买 (buy)
produce.gloss: Wǒ méi mǎi — I didn't buy (it).

cards.grammarNote: Feelings and states like 喜欢 take **不**; a completed action takes **没**.

contrast.prompt: Preference vs completed

a.gloss: Wǒ bù xǐhuān — I don't like (it)

b.gloss: Wǒ méi qù — I didn't go

cards.grammarNote: **别 + verb** = a negative command: 别哭 (don't cry), 别去 (don't go).

produce.concept: 别 + verb = Don't! (telling someone not to do something).
produce.task: tell someone 'Don't cry' with 哭 (cry)
produce.gloss: Bié kū — Don't cry.

cards.grammarNote: 别 tells someone NOT to do something. 别担心 = don't worry.
**不** states a fact about yourself; **别** tells someone else not to do it.

contrast.prompt: 'I don't…' vs 'Don't you…!'

a.gloss: Wǒ bù qù — I'm not going (statement)

b.gloss: Bié qù! — Don't go! (command)

cards.grammarNote: Pick by meaning: general 不, completed/有 没, command 别.

table.title: The three negators
rows: habits, adjectives, future — 不吃, 不好
completed actions & 'have' — 没吃, 没有
table.note: Pick by meaning: general 不, completed/有 没, command 别.

cards.grammarNote: Chinese needs a **measure word** between a number (or 这/那) and a noun. You can't say 两苹果 — you need **两个苹果**.

table.title: Number + measure word + noun
table.note: The measure word sits between the number and the noun: 两个苹果.

cards.grammarNote: **个** is the general measure word — use it when you don't know a more specific one. Works for people and most objects.

produce.concept: 个 is the default measure word for people and things.
produce.task: say 'three people' with 人 (person)
produce.gloss: sān gè rén — three people (number + 个 + noun)

cards.grammarNote: **杯** counts drinks served in a cup or glass: 一杯咖啡, 两杯茶.

cards.english: 只 for animals & paired body parts
cards.grammarNote: **只** counts many animals and paired body parts like hands, eyes and ears: 两只手, 一只眼睛.

produce.concept: 只 counts animals and paired body parts (hands, eyes, ears).
produce.task: say 'two eyes' with 眼睛 (eye)
produce.gloss: liǎng zhī yǎnjing — two eyes

cards.grammarNote: **张** counts flat things with a surface: maps, tables, paper, tickets: 一张地图, 一张桌子.
**本** counts bound volumes — books, notebooks, menus: 三本书, 一本菜单.

table.title: 本 — bound volumes
rows: 一本菜单 yì běn càidān
table.note: 本 counts anything bound like a book.

cards.grammarNote: **位** is a polite measure word for people you respect — guests, customers, professionals: 一位医生, 三位顾客.

contrast.prompt: Polite or neutral measure word for a person?

a.gloss: yí wèi yīshēng — a doctor (polite)

b.gloss: yí gè rén — a person (neutral)

cards.grammarNote: **条** counts long, thin, winding things: fish, streets, legs: 一条鱼, 一条街道.
**块** counts pieces or chunks (cake, chocolate) and is the everyday word for money: 一块蛋糕, 十块钱.

produce.concept: 块 counts chunks/pieces, and is the spoken measure for money.
produce.task: say 'a piece of cake' with 蛋糕 (cake)
produce.gloss: yí kuài dàngāo — a piece of cake

cards.grammarNote: **家** counts businesses and establishments: restaurants, stores, hotels: 一家餐厅, 两家商店.

cards.english: 这/那/哪 also take a measure word
cards.grammarNote: **这/那/哪** need a measure word too: 这个人, 那本书, 哪个. That's why 'this' is usually 这**个**.

table.title: Demonstrative + measure word + noun
rows: 这个人 zhège rén — this person
那本书 nà běn shū — that book
table.note: 这/那/哪 behave like a number — they still need a measure word.

cards.grammarNote: **几** (how many, for small numbers) also takes a measure word: 几个人？ 几本书？

cards.english: 两 vs 二 before a measure word
cards.grammarNote: Use **两** (not 二) for 'two' before a measure word: 两个, 两杯. 二 is for counting and in bigger numbers (十二).

contrast.prompt: Which 'two' goes before a measure word?

a.gloss: liǎng gè — two (of something) ✓

b.gloss: èr — the digit two / in 十二 (twelve)

cards.grammarNote: **多少** asks 'how much/many' for any amount and needs no measure word: 多少钱？ **几** is for small counts and takes a measure word.

contrast.prompt: Big/unknown amount, or a small count?

a.gloss: duōshǎo qián — how much money? (no measure word)

b.gloss: jǐ gè rén — how many people? (+ measure word)

cards.english: common measure words at a glance
cards.word: 个 / 杯 / 只 / 张
cards.grammarNote: Pick the measure word that fits the noun; **个** is the safe default when unsure.

table.title: Common measure words
table.note: When you don't know the right measure word, 个 usually works.

packs.name: 比 · 没有 · 一样 · 最 — Comparisons

cards.grammarNote: **A 比 B + adjective** = A is more (adj) than B. No 很 and no 是 — just the plain adjective after B.

table.title: A 比 B + adjective
rows: 比你 bǐ nǐ — than you
table.note: 我比你大 = I'm bigger / older than you.

cards.grammarNote: Order is always **A 比 B + adjective**.

produce.concept: A 比 B + adjective states A outranks B on that quality.
produce.task: say 'coffee is hotter than tea' with 咖啡, 茶, 热 (hot)
produce.gloss: Kāfēi bǐ chá rè — coffee is hotter than tea.

cards.grammarNote: A common mistake: don't put **很** in a 比 sentence. 很 means 'very' and clashes with the comparison.

contrast.prompt: Which 比 sentence is correct?

a.gloss: Wǒ bǐ nǐ dà — I'm older than you ✓

b.gloss: no 很 allowed in a 比 sentence ✗

cards.english: by how much? 一点 / 得多
cards.grammarNote: Add the amount after the adjective: **一点** (a little), **得多** (much more). Say it at the end, not before the adjective.

table.title: Adding degree to a 比 comparison
rows: 我比你大一点 — a little older
我比你大得多 — much older
table.note: The amount goes after the adjective: 大一点, 大得多.

cards.english: A 没有 B = not as … as
cards.grammarNote: **A 没有 B + adjective** = A is not as (adj) as B. It's the natural opposite of 比.

contrast.prompt: Two ways to say the same ranking

a.gloss: Wǒ méiyǒu nǐ dà — I'm not as old as you

b.gloss: Nǐ bǐ wǒ dà — you're older than me

cards.grammarNote: Use **没有** (not 不比) for 'not as … as'.

cloze.prompt: this restaurant isn't as big as that one

cards.phraseRomanized: Zhè jiā cāntīng méiyǒu nà jiā dà.
cards.englishPhrase: This restaurant isn't as big as that one.

cards.english: A 跟 B 一样 = the same as
cards.grammarNote: **A 跟 B 一样** = A is the same as B. Add an adjective for 'equally (adj)': 一样大 = equally big.

table.title: A 跟 B 一样 (+ adjective)
rows: 我跟你一样 — I'm the same as you
table.note: 跟 here means 'as / with'; 和 works too.

cards.grammarNote: Structure: **A 跟 B 一样 + adjective**.

produce.concept: 跟 … 一样 + adjective = equal on that quality.
produce.task: say 'I'm the same age/size as him' with 他 and 大
produce.gloss: Wǒ gēn tā yíyàng dà — I'm the same age as him.

cards.grammarNote: **更 + adjective** = even more (adj), compared with an implied standard: 这个更好 = this one is even better.
**很** just says 'very' (no comparison). **更** says 'even more' than something else.

contrast.prompt: Plain 'very', or 'even more'?

a.gloss: hěn hǎo — very good

b.gloss: gèng hǎo — even better

cards.grammarNote: **最 + adjective** = the most (adj), the superlative: 最好 = best, 最大 = biggest.

produce.concept: 最 + adjective = the most (superlative).
produce.task: say 'this one is the best' with 这个 and 好
produce.gloss: Zhège zuì hǎo — this one is the best.

cards.grammarNote: Use **最** for '-est / most'.
**最** works with verbs of feeling too: 最喜欢 = like best.

produce.concept: 最 + 喜欢 = like the most / favorite.
produce.task: say 'I like this one best' with 我, 喜欢, 这个
produce.gloss: Wǒ zuì xǐhuān zhège — I like this one best.

cards.word: 比 / 没有 / 一样 / 最
cards.grammarNote: Four building blocks: more (比), less (没有), equal (一样), most (最).

table.title: Comparison patterns
rows: A 比 B 大 — A is bigger
A 没有 B 大 — A is not as big
A 跟 B 一样大 — equally big
table.note: 比 and 没有 are opposites; 一样 means equal; 最 is the superlative.

cards.grammarNote: A **complement** attaches to a verb to say how it turned out. **吃完** = eat + finished = eat up.

table.title: Verb + result complement
table.note: The complement tells the outcome of the action.

cards.grammarNote: **完** after a verb = finished doing it: 吃完 (finish eating), 做完 (finish doing), 看完 (finish reading/watching).

produce.concept: Verb + 完 = complete the action.
produce.task: say 'I finished eating' with 吃 (eat) and 饭 (rice/meal)
produce.gloss: Wǒ chī wán fàn le — I finished my meal (了 confirms it's done).

cards.grammarNote: **到** after a verb marks reaching a result: 找到 (find), 看到 (manage to see), 买到 (succeed in buying).

cloze.prompt: I found it (searching reached its result)

cards.grammarNote: **见** is a result complement for perception: 看 = look (the action), 看见 = see (the result). Same with 听 / 听见.

contrast.prompt: The action, or the result achieved?

a.gloss: look (the action itself)

b.gloss: see (looking succeeded)

cards.english: 得 / 不 = can / can't reach the result
cards.grammarNote: Insert **得** (can) or **不** (cannot) between the verb and its complement: 看得见 (can see), 看不见 (can't see).

table.title: Potential complement: 得 (can) / 不 (cannot)
table.note: 得 = able to reach the result; 不 = not able to.

cards.grammarNote: Use **不** between verb and complement for 'cannot': 吃不完 = can't finish (too much to eat).

cloze.prompt: there's too much — I can't finish eating it

cards.grammarNote: **来** = motion toward the speaker; **去** = motion away. Add them to a verb to show direction: 进来, 进去.

table.title: Directional complements 来 / 去
rows: toward the speaker — 进来 come in
away from speaker — 进去 go in
table.note: 来 pulls toward 'me'; 去 pushes away from 'me'.

cards.grammarNote: Same verb 进 (enter), opposite viewpoint: 进来 if it's toward you, 进去 if it's away from you.

contrast.prompt: Coming toward me, or going away from me?

a.gloss: come in (toward the speaker)

b.gloss: go in (away from the speaker)

cards.grammarNote: **出去** = go out (away from the speaker). 出来 = come out (toward the speaker).
Stack a manner-of-motion verb before the direction: 跑出去 (run out), 走进来 (walk in).

produce.concept: manner verb + directional complement = how + which way.
produce.task: say 'he ran out' with 跑 (run) and 出去
produce.gloss: Tā pǎo chūqù le — he ran out (跑 + 出去).

cards.grammarNote: **上来** = come up (toward the speaker); 上去 = go up (away).
**Verb + 得 + adjective** describes how well the action is done: 说得很好 = speaks very well.

table.title: Degree complement: Verb + 得 + adjective
rows: 得很好 de hěn hǎo — very well
shuō de hěn hǎo — speaks very well
table.note: 得 links the verb to a comment on how it's performed.

cards.grammarNote: Structure: **Verb + 得 + 很 + adjective**.

produce.concept: Verb + 得 + adjective rates the performance of the action.
produce.task: say 'she eats a lot' with 吃 (eat) and 多 (much)
produce.gloss: Tā chī de hěn duō — she eats a lot.

cards.grammarNote: The linker between verb and its rating is **得**.
Both sound like 'de'. **得** rates an action (说得很好). **的** shows possession or links an adjective to a noun (我的书).

contrast.prompt: Rating an action, or marking possession?

a.gloss: shuō de hěn hǎo — speaks well (得 = how)

b.gloss: wǒ de shū — my book (的 = whose)

cards.grammarNote: Complements attach to a verb to add an outcome, a direction, or a rating.

table.title: Complements at a glance
table.note: Result = outcome; direction = which way; 得 = how well.

cards.english: 把 moves the object before the verb
cards.grammarNote: **把** pulls the object in front of the verb to spotlight what happens TO it: **Subject + 把 + object + verb + result**.

table.title: 把 sentence structure
rows: 把苹果 bǎ píngguǒ — the apple
吃了 chī le — ate (it up)
table.note: 我把苹果吃了 = I ate the apple (up).

cards.grammarNote: Use **把** when you want to stress what was done to a specific object — how it was dealt with, disposed of, or changed.

contrast.prompt: Neutral statement, or focus on the object's fate?

a.gloss: Wǒ chī le píngguǒ — I ate an apple (neutral)

b.gloss: Wǒ bǎ píngguǒ chī le — I ate the apple up (what happened to it)

cards.english: 把 needs more than a bare verb
cards.grammarNote: A **把** verb can't stand alone — add 了 or a complement to show the result: 把饭吃完 (finish the rice), not just 把饭吃.

table.title: 把 verbs take an extra element
rows: 把苹果吃了 — ate it up
把饭吃完 — finish the rice
table.note: The verb needs 了 or a complement so there's a clear outcome.

cards.grammarNote: **把 + object + 给 + person** is the natural way to ask someone to pass you something.

produce.concept: 把 + object + 给我 = hand the object to me.
produce.task: say 'please give me the menu' with 菜单 (menu) and 给我
produce.gloss: Qǐng bǎ càidān gěi wǒ — please give me the menu.

cards.grammarNote: The doer + **把** + object + verb + 了.
把 pairs naturally with a result complement like 完.

produce.concept: 把 + object + verb + complement.
produce.task: say 'finish the rice' with 饭 (rice) and 吃完 (finish eating)
produce.gloss: Bǎ fàn chī wán — finish (eating) the rice.

cards.grammarNote: Same handing-over pattern: 请 + 把 + object + 给我.
把 = you act ON an object and something happens to it.

table.title: 把 — disposal construction
rows: Subj + 把 + Obj + Verb + 了/complement
我把苹果吃了 — I ate the apple
table.note: The object is known/specific; the verb must show a result.

cards.grammarNote: **被** makes a passive: the subject receives the action. **Subject + 被 (+ doer) + verb + result**.

table.title: 被 sentence structure
rows: 吃了 chī le — was eaten
table.note: 苹果被吃了 = the apple was eaten.

cards.grammarNote: Name the doer right after **被**: 被他吃了 = eaten by him.

produce.concept: Subject + 被 + doer + verb + 了.
produce.task: say 'the coffee was drunk by him' with 咖啡, 他, 喝了
produce.gloss: Kāfēi bèi tā hē le — the coffee was drunk by him.

cards.grammarNote: You can drop the doer after **被** when it's unknown or unimportant: 苹果被吃了.

contrast.prompt: Doer left out, or named?

a.gloss: Píngguǒ bèi chī le — the apple was eaten (by someone)

b.gloss: Píngguǒ bèi tā chī le — the apple was eaten by him

cards.grammarNote: Receiver + **被** + verb + complement.
被 works with a result complement like 找到 (find).
cards.phraseRomanized: Wǒ de qián bèi zhǎodào le.

cards.english: 把 vs 被 — two viewpoints
cards.grammarNote: Same event, opposite starting point: **把** starts from the doer; **被** starts from the receiver.

contrast.prompt: Doer's view or receiver's view?

a.gloss: Tā bǎ píngguǒ chī le — he ate the apple (doer first)

b.gloss: Píngguǒ bèi tā chī le — the apple was eaten by him (receiver first)

cards.english: 把 and 被 at a glance
cards.grammarNote: Both restructure the sentence around an object, and both need the verb to carry 了 or a complement.

table.title: 把 vs 被
rows: 我把苹果吃了 — I ate the apple
苹果被吃了 — the apple was eaten
table.note: 把 = doer acts on object; 被 = object is acted upon.
